key_insight: During propeller speed changes at low Reynolds numbers, inflow remains largely quasi-steady while wake dynamics vary strongly and thrust exhibits hysteresis.
engineering_relevance: Steady-state thrust maps may misestimate transient thrust in small UAVs, even when nondimensional acceleration suggests negligible unsteady effects.
method: Tested a two-bladed propeller in hover at pitch offsets of 0°, 5°, and 10°.
Applied open-loop acceleration and deceleration steps between 3000 and 5000 RPM.
Combined load measurements with phase-locked PIV at three radial stations and in the meridian plane.
evidence_signal: At the 5° pitch offset, thrust-coefficient deviations from steady values reached 8% during acceleration and 5% during deceleration; wake deviations were largest at low RPM.
watch_item: The abstract inconsistently describes the 10° case as both quasi-steady and hysteretic; verify pitch-dependent conclusions in the full paper before implementation.
paper_title: On the aerodynamics of an accelerating and decelerating propeller in hover at low Reynolds numbers
